payload.description:
The worker Dockerfile installs '.[all]', which pulls the full ML training stack (torch, transformers, sentence-transformers, gensim, bertopic, umap-learn, hdbscan, shap, numba/llvmlite, tables, datasets, kaleido) into a container that only scores. Empirically verified in a clean venv: the scoring API worker (full import chain incl. LangGraphScore/TactusScore/nodes), all 15 worker tests, and the plexus predict CLI work with core + infra + a small subset: pandas, scikit-learn, nltk, seaborn, graphviz, pydot, contractions. The only blockers for dropping the rest are module-level xgboost/imblearn imports in plexus/cli/data/operations.py serving the 'plexus data' training command. Expected effect: roughly 1.5-2 GB smaller Linux image, faster builds, and removal of the CPU-Torch preinstall workaround.

Plan:
1. Add a 'scoring' extra to pyproject.toml with the verified subset.
2. Make xgboost/imblearn imports lazy inside the plexus data command paths.
3. Dockerfile installs '.[scoring,infra]' and drops the Torch preinstall ARGs/line; NLTK data download stays.
4. Keep 'all' unchanged for training/EC2 use.

```gherkin
Feature: Slim scoring worker dependencies
  Scenario: Scoring worker runs without training packages
    Given a Plexus installation with only the scoring and infra extras
    When the scoring API worker and the plexus predict CLI load
    Then no torch-family or training-only packages are required

  Scenario: CLI loads without training packages
    Given xgboost and imbalanced-learn are not installed
    When the plexus CLI module tree loads
    Then loading succeeds and only invoking the data training commands requires those packages
```

Validation: new failing test first (CLI data module imports with xgboost/imblearn blocked), full focused suite, poetry check, plexus --help in a venv without training packages, and a Docker image build comparing size against the previous local image. Final end-to-end proof remains the kind/Envoy POC scoring request.
payload.title: Worker image installs scoring dependency set without ML training stack
